newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU denies legal action against gelatine producers.
newsitem.headline: EU denies legal action against gelatine producers.

text.p: The European Commission denied on Thursday a newspaper report that it had decided to take European gelatine manufacturers to court for withholding important information on mad cow disease.

The French daily Le Monde said in its Friday edition that EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler had told it he had decided to take legal action because the manufacturers did not promptly pass on new data raising doubts about the safety of new gelatine production methods.
"There's no decision yet. Fischler is still looking to see it it's possible," a Fischler aide told Reuters.
On June 11, the European Commission agreed to lift the ban on gelatine, a beef by-product widely used in food, cosmetics and medicinal products, if stricter heat-processing rules were respected.
The rules were intended to ensure that the Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) agent was eradicated.
But on June 14 the Gelatine Manufacturers of Europe handed over a new report saying more research was needed before the safety of the new processing techniques could be guaranteed.
The manufacturers had the new report on April 10 but did not pass it on, Fischler's aide said, adding that this was unacceptable.
The EU imposed a worldwide ban on British beef exports in March after the British government triggered a massive public health scare by disclosing that BSE could be passed to humans.

Around 165,000 British cattle have been struck down by the fatal cattle brain disease over the past 10 years, compared with less than 1,000 in other European countries. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
